messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: spike in 5xx for /v1/stream (hosted) from 09:11 UTC, affected p95 latency and streaming connections. Auto-scaling OK. Paging oncall.

ashley (oncall): on it, paging into channel. any customer reports yet?

rachel (cs): got a report from Acme at 09:12, they say streaming sessions drop immediately after handshake when using client v0.13. "clients start receiving EOF". Ticket #INC-4987.

ashley (oncall): ack. matt? mateo, jin — can you triage connection failures + recent deploys?

mateo: looking. quick glance at canary rollout history: SDK-proxy image bumped to 0.13.0 and rolled to 10% at 09:10 via canary pipeline. deploy-bot shows rollout id: r-20250303-1210.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout r-20250303-1210: started 09:10 UTC -> 10% -> health checks passed initially.

jin: I see streams failing in logs: backend responds 101 then client closes with RST. Error shows "unexpected frame" in our stream parser. Reproducing locally against canary shows framing change: client now sends `:ctrl` preface byte that we didn't expect.

mateo: that sounds like client incompat. Is 0.13 supposed to be wire-compatible? I thought we had contract tests.

jin: 0.13 introduced a new keepalive preface (single 0x1E) for background clients; server should accept but our parser treats unknown control bytes as fatal.

ashley (oncall): this is a contract break in deployed proxy path. What's customer impact? rachel?

rachel (cs): Acme saw 100% broken streams. Several other customers on canary group report intermittent disconnects. No data lost for non-stream endpoints.

ops-sre: SLO alert triggered for 5xx + dropped connections. Incident severity = sev2 (partial outage for streaming API).

ashley (oncall): propose immediate mitigation: flip feature-flag that enables new keepalive/wire-mode to false (kill-switch) for canary and rollback canary image if flag flip insufficient. Who can flip flag?

mateo: I can flip the feature flag in launchdarkly. Flag key: streaming_new_preface_v0_13. Command in console only. I'll do it now and monitor.

mateo: (after) flipped streaming_new_preface_v0_13 -> false for all canary environments at 09:18 UTC.

jin: after flag flip, canary logs show old framing accepted again, connection drops drop by ~80%. Some long-lived clients immediately reconnect and recover.

rachel (cs): Acme confirms they can reconnect successfully. "Looks good from our side".

ashley (oncall): good quick mitigation. But we need rollback plan. Is canary rollback straightforward?

deploy-bot: Canary rollback command available: `deploy rollback r-20250303-1210 --to-image sha:abc123`

mateo: I'll coordinate rollback to image before 0.13 (sha:abc122). Rolling back canary to 0% -> 0.12 at 09:26.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated 09:26 UTC. Progress: 10% -> 0% for 0.13.

jin: keep monitoring logs and SLOs. Also opening a regression PR to make parser tolerant of unknown control bytes (non-fatal) so future clients don't break us.

ashley (oncall): action items: 1) Temporary: feature flag kill-switch already flipped (mateo). 2) Rollback canary complete (deploy-bot). 3) Patch parser to tolerate new preface (jin). 4) Postmortem + notify customers (rachel).
Please confirm ownership.

rachel (cs): I'll send customer update template and reach out to Acme and other affected customers. Will include timeline and mitigation.

ops-sre: rollback completed at 09:29 UTC -> 0.13 removed from canary. Global traffic not affected. 5xx and drop metrics trending back to baseline by 09:35.

mateo: noting root cause: SDK 0.13 shipped new keepalive preface without proper backward-compatible handshake; server parser treated unknown byte as fatal. We missed this in contract tests because contract harness didn't include keepalive preface vectors.

jin: patch PR opened: github.com/redwood/streaming-parser/pull/421. Fix: treat unknown control bytes as neutral -> log + ignore. Add fuzz vectors for preface variations.

ashley (oncall): great. Next steps before closing incident: a) test and roll fix to prod, b) add contract tests and gating for future SDK bumps, c) schedule a postmortem doc and retro. Targets?

jin: will prioritize patch, aim for canary deploy of parser fix by EOD (2025-03-03) and full rollout tomorrow morning.

mateo: I'll add gating to the SDK release checklist: new wire changes must include wire-compat vectors and server/SDK cross-test.

rachel (cs): customer comms drafted, sending now. Will keep affected customers posted once fix is deployed.

ashley (oncall): closing loop: all mitigation steps executed. Monitoring will stay in this thread until metrics stable for 2 hours. If anything else, ping @ashley or escalate to eng-sre channel. Thanks team :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident INC-4987 updated: severity -> sev2 -> mitigated. Timeline and actions recorded.

ashley (oncall): final note — follow-up postmortem assigned to jin + mateo + rachel. Please include timeline, RCA, and checklist updates.

mateo: ack, will add release gating item and draft the postmortem by tomorrow.

jin: ack. I'll include unit/regression tests and the PR link.

rachel (cs): I'll attach customer notifications & impact summary.

ashley (oncall): closing thread at 11:11 UTC once metrics stable. Thanks all.
